OPEN COMMAND

Standard play. Full meter visibility, rewind available.

WHERE THE WAR IS AT

July 1941. Japan has just occupied southern Indochina, and how strictly Washington enforces the resulting freeze on Japanese assets is still a honestly open administrative question. This command is about to help answer it, for better or worse.

"Yesterday, December 7, 1941, a date which will live in infamy."

— PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT

Historically accurate opponent. Unchecked, a small number of genuinely contested moments this campaign touches may play out differently than they did historically — discovered in play, never announced in advance.

A PLUS READING MEANS BETTER SUPPLIED AND RUNNING AHEAD OF SCHEDULE. A MINUS READING MEANS THE REVERSE.

A war that confirmed Europe First at Arcadia, and fought a honestly different middle, a declined Midway ambush, or every Central Pacific atoll taken by direct assault instead of bypassed, converges back toward its historical shape at the finish anyway. The bomb, the Soviet declaration, and Japan's cabinet deadlock land almost exactly when they actually did, largely indifferent to which operational road got the fleet to 1945. What changed, put plainly on the record rather than left in this fleet's own files, sits beside the documented total for this theater, a little over 111,000 American dead: not a different destination, but a real, countable addition to or subtraction from that number, depending on which road actually got walked.

THE DICE YOU ROLLED

This war passed through 1 contested outcome. The compound likelihood of the exact path you walked: ~70%. Portions of this path are marked speculative: the odds above are a statement of how far it stands from what the evidence supports.

COMMAND TIMELINE · 8 DIVERGENCES FROM THE RECORD
SCORECARD VS. HISTORY · MATCHED 7/11, OUT-POSITIONED 1/11
DECISION LOG
JULY 1941 — Make the total embargo an explicit, publicly announced presidential decision rather than an administrative drift
DECEMBER 1941 — Recall the relief force: preserve Saratoga and her escort rather than risk them against a force already converging on the island
DECEMBER 1941 – JANUARY 1942 — Affirm Europe First: the Pacific gets a defensive minimum while the main weight goes to the Atlantic
FEBRUARY 1942 — Reject the removal order: side with the Justice Department's objection, pursue individualized security review instead
MARCH – APRIL 1942 — Commit the Chinese divisions to an absolute defense of Rangoon (A harder defeat, not a saved city)
FEBRUARY 1942 — Defy Churchill: insist
